name: Auditory Scene Analysis Demand
higher_order_principle: Complex acoustic environments with multiple concurrent sources (speech, noise, machinery) impose computational load on the auditory system to parse and segregate streams (auditory scene analysis). This consumes cognitive resources, depleting the capacity available for concurrent tasks like reading, conversation, or creative thinking.

parameters.bold_scaling: ~5% increase per additional source up to capacity

scope_conditions: Applies to environments with multiple concurrent sound sources
Fails when sources are spectrotemporally identical (cannot segregate)
Degraded in hearing-impaired and older (>60y) populations

interactions.description: If ASA fails to segregate a source, or if a source is identified as threatening, it triggers the HPA axis (T5).
ASA demand draws from the same general cognitive resource pool as Working Memory (T36).

key_references: Bregman, A. S. (1990). Auditory Scene Analysis.
McDermott, J. H. (2009). The cocktail party problem. Current Biology.
Szalma, J. L., & Hancock, P. A. (2011). Noise effects on human performance. Psychological Bulletin.
